senses.sense_definition: To stunt, inhibit progress, or make dull and uninteresting, especially through restrictive routine or excessive bureaucracy.

examples.text: Bureaucracy and excessive over-regulation have <w>stultified</w> the country's economic growth.
Monotonous factory routines often <w>stultify</w> the creative minds of young workers.

senses.sense_definition: To render ineffective, useless, or completely worthless.

examples.text: His entire business model was <w>stultified</w> by rapid shifts in consumer technology.
The committee made a sudden rule change that threatened to <w>stultify</w> their previous agreements.

senses.sense_definition: To cause someone to appear foolish, ridiculous, or inconsistent, often used reflexively.

examples.text: The politician managed to <w>stultify</w> himself by completely contradicting his earlier remarks.
She refused to <w>stultify</w> her reputation by defending such an absurd proposal.

senses.sense_definition: To allege or prove that someone is of unsound mind or legally incompetent.

examples.text: Under traditional common law, a person could not legally plead to <w>stultify</w> himself to void a contract.
The lawyer attempted to <w>stultify</w> the defendant in order to invalidate the signed agreement.
